History and Development of the Company
We were originally formed on January 16, 2007 as a limited partnership named “Capital Product Partners L.P.” under the laws of the Marshall Islands. We completed our initial public offering in April 2007. On the Effective Date, we converted into a corporation named “Capital Clean Energy Carriers Corp.” organized under the laws of the Marshall Islands. We maintain our principal executive headquarters at 3 Iassonos Street, Piraeus, 18537 Greece and our telephone number is +30 210 4584 950. Our registered address in the Marshall Islands is Trust Company Complex, Ajeltake Road, Ajeltake Island, Majuro, Marshall Islands MH96960. The name of our registered agent at such address is The Trust Company of the Marshall Islands, Inc. Our website address is www.capitalcleanenergycarriers.com . The SEC maintains an internet website at www.sec.gov that contains reports and other information regarding issuers, including us, that file electronically with the SEC. The information contained on, or that can be accessed through these websites is not part of, and is not incorporated into, this Annual Report.
Developments in 2025 and up to the filing of this Annual Report
Vessel Acquisitions and Advances for Vessels Under Construction
On January 5, 2026, we took delivery of the LCO 2 – HMG/C Active. The LCO 2 – HMG/C Active is the first vessel in our Gas Fleet to be delivered to the Company and is the world’s first 22,000 CBM low-pressure LCO 2 carrier. The vessel commenced a six-month charter transporting LPG with Geogas Trading SA (“Geogas”), with an option to extend the charter for an additional six months. The acquisition of the LCO 2 – HMG/C Active was financed with $29.4 million of cash on hand and a 12-year loan of $48.9 million. The loan is repayable in 48 quarterly instalments of approximately $0.6 million, with a balloon payment of $18.0 million payable with the final instalment in December 2037. The Company may borrow an additional amount of up to $7.5 million if the vessel secures long term employment.
On December 29, 2025, we announced an investment in three latest technology LNG/C vessels to be built at Hyundai for a total contract price of $769.5 million, with expected deliveries in the third quarter of 2028 and the first quarter of 2029. In addition to $37.0 million that we have paid to-date, we expect to pay an additional amount of $707.0 million to Hyundai in pre-delivery and delivery installments.

Financing Arrangements
BGN Joint Venture
On April 15, 2026, we announced a joint venture arrangement with BMarine Shipping Investment FZCO (“BMarine”), an affiliate of global energy trader the BGN Group. Pursuant to the joint venture arrangement, we have agreed to sell the LNG/C Amore Mio I to BM Capital HoldCo LLC (the “BGN JV”), a newly formed Marshall Islands limited liability company in which we hold a 51% interest and BMarine holds the remaining 49%, for a purchase price of $230.0 million. In connection with the transaction, the LNG/C Amore Mio I will be chartered to BGN INT DMCC, an affiliate of BGN Group, under a 10-year time charter, with two three-year extension options exercisable by the charterer. Expected aggregate revenues under the charter are approximately $485.6 million if all extension options are exercised, with the charter period extending through 2043. We expect to close the transaction in the first quarter of 2027, at which time the existing financing on the vessel will be refinanced.

Information on the Company” for information on the current scope of our operations. We currently own 12 latest generation LNG/C vessels, one LCO 2 – HMG/C vessel and one legacy Neo-Panamax container carrier vessel. In addition, our Under Construction Fleet includes nine additional latest generation LNG/C vessels, six dual-fuel MG/C vessels and three LCO 2 – HMG/C vessels, to be delivered between the second quarter of 2026 and the first quarter of 2029. We may in the future enter into additional markets. If that happens, we will be exposed to additional risks.
If any of the following risks actually occurs, our business, financial condition, operating results and cash flow could be materially adversely affected. If that happens, we might not be able to pay dividends on our common shares, the trading price of our common shares could decline and you could lose all or part of your investment.
The risks described below include forward-looking statements and our actual results may differ substantially from those discussed in such forward-looking statements. For more information, please read “Forward Looking Statements” above.

SUMMARY OF RISK FACTORS
The following is a summary of some of the principal risks we face. The list below is not exhaustive, and you should read this “Risk factors” section in full.
·
The ocean-going LNG, LPG and container shipping industries are cyclical and volatile;
·
The wider energy transition gas market, such as the carriage of low carbon ammonia and LCO 2 , continues to develop and shipping demand, charter hire rates and profitability for this market are uncertain;
·
An oversupply of LNG/C, LPG carrier or containership capacity may depress current charter rates and adversely affect our ability to charter our vessels at profitable rates or at all;
·
We may not realize the benefits anticipated from our Under Construction Fleet;
·
We may not realize the benefits anticipated from our change in business focus to concentrate on the LNG/C market, the LPG carriage market and the wider energy transition gas market such as the carriage of low carbon ammonia and LCO 2 ;
·
Marine transportation is inherently risky, and an incident involving significant loss of, or environmental contamination by, any of our vessels could harm our reputation and business;
·
Political and government instability can affect the industries in which we operate, which may adversely affect our business;
·
We may not be able to grow our business or to effectively manage our growth;
·
Certain of our vessels may be under time charters at rates that are at a substantial premium to the spot and period markets, and our charterers’ failure to perform under these time charters could result in a significant loss of expected future revenues and cash flows;
·
We currently derive a significant part of our revenues from a limited number of charterers and the loss of any charterer or charter or vessel could result in a significant loss of revenues and cash flows;
·
A decrease in the level of export and import of goods or LNG, LPG or ammonia production and exports, as a result of trade protectionism, including threats or imposition of tariffs or other trade barriers, economic sanctions, changes in commodity prices or other factors affecting global markets, could affect demand for shipping;
·
Vessel values may decrease and over time may fluctuate substantially, which may cause us to recognize losses if we sell our vessels or record impairments and affect our ability to comply with our loan covenants or refinance our debt; and
·
An increase in interest rates or increased interest rate levels for long periods of time could increase our level of debt and the related interest expense, limit our ability to access debt and equity financing and increase the cost of capital required to acquire additional vessels or to implement our business strategy.

RISKS RELATED TO OUR INDUSTRY
We are exposed to various risks in the ocean-going LNG, LPG and container shipping industries, which are cyclical and volatile, and the wider energy transition gas market, which continues to develop.
As of the date of this Annual Report, we own 12 LNG/C vessels, one LCO 2 – HMG/C vessel and one legacy Neo-Panamax container carrier vessel. In addition, our Under Construction Fleet includes nine additional latest generation LNG/C vessels, six dual-fuel MG/C vessels and three LCO 2 – HMG/C vessels, to be delivered between the second quarter of 2026 and the first quarter of 2029.
Currently, the majority of our vessels operate in the LNG shipping industry and our performance and future growth depend on continued demand in this industry. The LNG shipping industry is cyclical with attendant volatility in charter hire rates and profitability. Charter hire rates for LNG/C vessels depend on multiple factors, including changes in the supply and demand for LNG and changes in the supply and demand for LNG shipping capacity. In recent years, the LNG/C charter market recovered after experiencing a prolonged period of historically low rates. However, beginning in 2023 charter rates began to decrease and in 2024 and 2025 charter rates were significantly lower compared to the prior year, due to an oversupplied freight market resulting from the mismatch between increased supply from vessel deliveries and decreased demand from delays in LNG projects. In 2025, charter rates were also negatively impacted by shorter voyage durations freeing up capacity due to strong European demand and weaker Asian demand. The degree of charter hire rate volatility among different types of LNG/C vessels has varied widely. In the past, there have been times when charter and spot market rates for LNG/C vessels declined below the operating costs of vessels.
Upon delivery of the LCO 2 – HMG/C Active, we have begun to operate in the LPG shipping industry, and in the future we expect to operate in the wider energy transition gas market, such as the carriage of low carbon ammonia and LCO 2 . Accordingly, we are exposed to the various risks in these industries and our exposure will increase as additional vessels that constitute the Gas Fleet are delivered to us. The wider energy transition gas market continues to develop and charter hire rates and profitability for this market are uncertain. In particular, large-scale markets for the carriage of low carbon ammonia and LCO 2 do not yet exist. Our performance and future growth depend on successful development of such markets. Significant investment by governments and industry, including subsidies in certain cases, in addition to regulatory changes, will be required to successfully develop large-scale markets for the carriage of low carbon ammonia and LCO 2 .
